note: Data-driven settings schema. Each entry declares how to read the LIVE value, where the PERSISTENT value lives, its DEFAULT and RECOMMENDED value (or range/choices), and - when safely editable - an edit descriptor (class sysctl|sysfs) for the admin-gated apply engine. Groups: safe | aggressive | tkg | info.

settings.title: vm.swappiness
settings.description: How aggressively the kernel swaps anonymous memory. On a 128GB workstation lower values keep app pages resident and reduce latency stalls that can trip browser watchdogs.
settings.rollback: Remove the entry from /etc/sysctl.d/ and run: sudo sysctl -w vm.swappiness=60

settings.title: fs.inotify.max_user_watches
settings.description: Max files a user can watch with inotify. VS Code / Electron file watchers exhaust the 65536 default on large trees, causing degraded behavior and crashes in some apps.
settings.rollback: Remove the entry from /etc/sysctl.d/; default restores on reboot.

settings.title: fs.inotify.max_user_instances
settings.description: Max inotify instances per user. Electron apps each hold several; the default of 128 can run out with many apps open.
settings.rollback: Remove the entry from /etc/sysctl.d/; default restores on reboot.

settings.title: vm.max_map_count
settings.description: Max memory-mapped areas per process. Modern browsers and Electron map thousands of regions; too low a value produces hard-to-diagnose crashes.
settings.rollback: Remove the entry from /etc/sysctl.d/; default restores on reboot.

settings.title: kernel.core_pattern
settings.description: Where core dumps go. Ubuntu pipes them to apport, which feeds /var/crash — keep this intact while diagnosing the Firefox/Electron crashes.
settings.rollback: Managed by apport.service; restart it to restore.

settings.title: systemd-oomd service
settings.description: Userspace OOM killer. Known to kill entire app slices (browser included) under memory pressure — a classic cause of 'silent' browser disappearance.
settings.rollback: sudo systemctl enable --now systemd-oomd

settings.title: oomd ManagedOOMSwap (root slice)
settings.description: Ubuntu's fix for the notorious 22.04 'oomd kills Firefox/VS Code' bug (LP #1972159) set ManagedOOMSwap=auto on -.slice. Expect 'auto'; 'kill' means the swap-kill misfire mode is active.
settings.rollback: Remove any local -.slice.d override; Ubuntu default is auto.

settings.title: MGLRU min_ttl_ms
settings.description: MGLRU anti-thrashing valve. Nonzero values protect the recent working set but invoke the kernel OOM killer to terminate apps when it can't stay resident — a candidate explanation for unexplained app deaths. Default 0 (disabled); such kills are logged in dmesg/journal.
settings.rollback: echo 0 | sudo tee /sys/kernel/mm/lru_gen/min_ttl_ms

settings.title: oomd DefaultMemoryPressureLimit
settings.description: Memory-pressure threshold above which systemd-oomd starts killing. Raising it (or the duration) makes oomd less trigger-happy on a big-RAM box.
settings.rollback: Comment the line out in /etc/systemd/oomd.conf and restart systemd-oomd.
settings.recommended: 60%; raise to 80% only after observed oomd kills

settings.title: vm.overcommit_memory
settings.description: Kernel overcommit policy. 0 = heuristic (default). Changing this affects how allocations fail versus how the OOM killer engages.
settings.rollback: sudo sysctl -w vm.overcommit_memory=0

settings.title: vm.min_free_kbytes
settings.description: Reserved free memory floor. Raising it gives the kernel headroom during allocation bursts (reduces atomic-allocation failures); too high wastes RAM and can trigger early reclaim.
settings.rollback: Remove the sysctl.d entry; reboot restores the auto-computed default.

settings.title: Transparent hugepages
settings.description: THP mode: always / madvise / never. 'always' can cause latency spikes and memory bloat in browsers; 'madvise' is the common stability recommendation.
settings.rollback: Remove transparent_hugepage= from GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT, update-grub, reboot.

settings.title: MGLRU (multi-gen LRU)
settings.description: Multi-generational LRU page reclaim. Bitmask in /sys/kernel/mm/lru_gen/enabled; improves reclaim behavior under pressure on recent kernels.
settings.rollback: echo the previous bitmask back, or reboot.
settings.recommended: 0x0007; A/B test off (n) for reclaim stalls

settings.title: Open-file limit (soft)
settings.description: Per-process file descriptor soft limit for the session. Electron apps with many IPC pipes and sockets can hit low limits.
settings.rollback: Comment the line out in /etc/systemd/system.conf; reboot.

settings.title: GPU kernel driver
settings.description: Which kernel driver drives the RTX 3060. nouveau on GA104 is a major crash source for browser GPU processes under Wayland; the proprietary/open NVIDIA driver is the usual stability fix.

argv: lspci -k | grep -A3 -i 'vga\|3d' | grep -m1 'Kernel driver in use' | sed 's/.*: //'

settings.rollback: ubuntu-drivers / apt manage driver packages.

settings.title: Kernel command line
settings.description: Boot parameters. Live value is what the running kernel booted with; persistent is GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT in /etc/default/grub.
settings.rollback: Edit /etc/default/grub, sudo update-grub, reboot.

settings.title: Swap devices
settings.description: Active swap. Currently an 8G swapfile and no zram; zram is a common recommendation to smooth memory pressure spikes.
settings.rollback: n/a (informational)
settings.recommended: keep swap present - systemd-oomd requires it

settings.title: Running kernel
settings.description: Kernel release currently booted.
settings.rollback: Select another kernel from the GRUB menu.

settings.title: linux-tkg kernel installed
settings.description: Whether a linux-tkg custom kernel is present in /boot. The tkg section of the tuning report covers building one (scheduler choice, config options, DKMS caveats).
settings.rollback: Boot the stock Ubuntu kernel from GRUB; remove tkg packages.

settings.title: BORE scheduler
settings.description: kernel.sched_bore exists only on kernels built with the BORE scheduler (a common linux-tkg choice). Absent on stock Ubuntu EEVDF kernels.
settings.rollback: n/a (kernel build option)

settings.title: Preemption model
settings.description: PREEMPT_DYNAMIC on stock Ubuntu; linux-tkg builds often use full preempt. Boot-time selectable via preempt= on dynamic kernels.
settings.rollback: Remove preempt= from the kernel command line.

settings.title: Shared Electron runtime
settings.description: Version at /opt/electron used by the jobs app and claude-desktop. Electron 44 / Chromium 152's GPU process fails on the nouveau/NVK+zink stack until fallback exhaustion FATALs the app (SIGTRAP crashes of 2026-08-26).
settings.rollback: Reinstall a different version via the install-electron job.
settings.recommended: latest stable on the nvidia driver

settings.title: KMS drivers per card
settings.description: Kernel driver behind each DRM card. card0 (RTX 3060) drives the GNOME session; Chromium renders via ANGLE→zink→NVK on top of it.

argv: for c in /sys/class/drm/card[0-9]; do echo "$(basename $c): $(basename $(readlink $c/device/driver))"; done | paste -sd ', '

settings.rollback: n/a (informational)
settings.recommended: nvidia-drm atomic on the display GPU

settings.title: apport crash capture
settings.description: Keeps /var/crash dumps flowing — the mechanism that let us extract the Electron FATAL. Leave active while diagnosing.
settings.rollback: sudo systemctl enable --now apport

settings.title: Open-file limit (hard)
settings.description: Per-process fd hard limit for the session. Note: cockpit-bridge sessions report their own limits, which can differ from desktop/terminal sessions.
settings.rollback: Comment the line out in /etc/systemd/system.conf; reboot.

settings.title: Kernel taint flags
settings.description: 0 = untainted. Nonzero after loading out-of-tree modules (e.g. the NVIDIA driver sets taint bits) or kernel warnings/oopses — useful context when reading crash-era journals.
settings.rollback: n/a (informational)

settings.title: THP defrag mode
settings.description: How aggressively the kernel compacts memory for hugepages. 'always' can stall allocations; 'madvise' or 'defer+madvise' are the usual desktop settings.
settings.rollback: echo the previous mode back, or reboot.

settings.title: vm.watermark_scale_factor
settings.description: Distance between kswapd wake-up watermarks (units of 0.01% of RAM). Raising it starts background reclaim earlier, smoothing pressure spikes at the cost of more background work.
settings.rollback: sudo sysctl -w vm.watermark_scale_factor=10

settings.title: Timer frequency (CONFIG_HZ)
settings.description: Kernel tick rate. Stock Ubuntu uses 1000Hz on recent releases; linux-tkg offers 500/750/1000. Build-time only.
settings.rollback: n/a (kernel build option)
